mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.5pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 2% year-over-year, it signals a period of accommodative monetary policy with inflationary pressures, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a single month, coupled with an unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5%, signals a weakening labor market and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases > 100k in 1 month and UNRATE > 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS decreases > 100k in 1 month and UNRATE > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% year-over-year signals a strengthening demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances where HOUST increases > 10% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a single month, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% in 1 month.
